The issue number 787 is not printed on the article's pages nor in the IA or Zenodo metadata, and the BHL part page (biodiversitylibrary.org/part/186771) refused the script (403): the issue number is unverified, not known to be wrong

claims.claim: watershield in a New Hampshire pond began growing on 24–25 April
claims.quote: the remaining nine plants germinated within a two day period, April 24 and 25
claims.conditions: Wheelwright Pond, Lee, NH (43°08′N; 100+ acres, 1–30 ft deep), 1966; 10 tagged plants observed daily 11–30 April, one failed to grow; 'germination' = the first winterbud meristem elongated one inch; confirmed at the pond's three other stations and at the Nottingham beaver pond

claims.quote: clearly destined to become overwintering structures were collected on July 30, 1966
claims.conditions: 1966; the date the first buds clearly destined to overwinter were collected. Adams notes the start of winterbud formation is hard to date because every growing apex looks like a one-segment winterbud all season; the winterbud-development curve counts buds on 20 random plants weekly from 23 July to 28 September (p. 422)

claims.quote: Thirty-five percent of the total production overwintered and in the attached condition
claims.conditions: 1966 season, > 6,000 winterbuds counted 1966–67; the 60 % that matured and floated free before 1 October all died; of the 40 % still attached on 1 October, 35 % of total production overwintered attached, 4 % floated free and died at icing-in, 1 % survived entangled; fewer than 0.25 % of production had any potential to survive once freed

claims.claim: "no individual plant lasts more than one season" (given as a quotation of Adams)
claims.source_value: Adams's words are "no single individual will be more than one season old" (the colonies are perennial; no rhizome segment is more than two seasons old)
claims.quote: no single individual will be more than one season old
claims.note: the meaning is right, but the paper puts a paraphrase in quotation marks; quote Adams's own words or drop the quotation marks

claims.claim: watershield: ramets living one season, the clone carried by its winter buds (Adams 1969)
claims.quote: attached overwintering winterbud structure is, in fact, absolutely essential for the annual survival
claims.conditions: the clone is carried by the buds that stay ATTACHED to the parent rhizome over winter; buds that float free are 'an ineffective agent of vegetative reproduction' in these ponds
claims.note: 'small oval pads' in the same comment is not from Adams (the paper does not describe the leaves)

notes: An earlier fetch had indexed the IA djvu.txt (HTML); this pass re-indexed the IA PDF so pages can be cited and figures seen. Other values useful to the model: winterbud germination fails below a 'compensation depth' between six and seven feet (p. 425, Fig. 4 experiment); 'Winterbuds can not withstand freezing' — any freezing of the meristem prevented germination (p. 425); freed buds sank once their mucilage halved, and those germinating precociously in autumn did so at the same day length as the spring germination (p. 426). Fig. 2 (p. 420) plots water temperature, day length, the leaf growth curve (peaking around early July), flowering and the winterbud and decay curves for 1966.
